exposure: Compound heterozygous mutations in the SLC26A2 gene (splice site variant c.-26+2T > C and missense variant c.1957T > A (p.Cys653Ser) for Patient I; missense variants c.835C > T (p.Arg279Trp) and c.1535C > A (p.Thr512Lys) for Patient II)
outcome: Cervical kyphosis with an underdeveloped C4
cohort: Two patients from non-consanguineous families presenting with recessive multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (rMED) due to very rare compound heterozygous mutation combinations in the SLC26A2 gene were reported.
finding: The study of these two patients further clarifies the variability in phenotypic and genetic presentations of recessive multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (rMED).
followup_time: For Patient I, 33 years; N/A for Patient II
